card.name: Small words in overdose section openings
card.fires_on: Short linking or qualifying words (of, to, acute, oral) in the first sentence or two of an OVERDOSAGE section, just before a drug name or overdose term. It also fires on odd spots like the F in CSF.

modes.label: LD50 phrasing
modes.description: The word 'of' right after 'oral LD 50' or 'intravenous LD 50', before the drug name.
modes.example: OVERDOSAGE: The oral LD 50<< of>> sulfacetamide in mice is 1

modes.label: Overdose presentation wording
modes.description: Qualifier words such as 'acute' or 'oral' near the start of an overdose description.
modes.example: 10 OVERDOSAGE Clinical Presentation The manifestations of<< acute>> overdose include pinpoint pupils, sedation,

modes.label: Linking word in treatment line
modes.description: The word 'to' in a sentence about symptoms attributed to the overdose.
modes.example: 10 OVERDOSAGE In case of an overdose, remove the topically applied product with soap and water, and treat the symptoms and signs attributed<< to>> the overdose symptomatically.

card.writes: It seems to push toward word beginnings like nit-, nic-, bor-, cit-, aspir-, creat-, which start chemical and drug names, and away from the word chemical.
card.plain: It marks the opening lines of an overdose section, where a drug name is likely to come next.
